subject: Multi-tenant cache interference & priority preemption causing stream stalls
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel@scitext.ai>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-06T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Sudden stream-start latency spikes, suspect multi-tenant interference

Hi Rafael —

We started seeing a regression this morning around 07:45 PST: stream start times went from ~200ms to 1.2–1.8s for ~40% of requests and a smaller population hit 5–10s. p95 and p99 both spiked, and we saw ~2% 5xxs correlating with the stalls. This is our prod tenant (scitext-main) on the hosted cluster in us-west-2.

I attached a small bundle (logs/kv_dump_20281106.tar.gz) with connection traces, the prefetch metrics CSV, and a few sample request IDs. The pattern looks like long tail waits where the model stream doesn't begin until KV hits return; CPU/GPU metrics look normal.

Can your team triage? This is customer-facing search and it's causing query failures in our pipelines. Happy to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Director, ML Ops
Scitext AI

Attachments: logs/kv_dump_20281106.tar.gz, prefetch-metrics-20281106.csv

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Park <daniel@scitext.ai>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-06T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden stream-start latency spikes, suspect multi-tenant interference

Thanks for the report, Daniel — we see the alerts. I’m looping in Ben from serving infra and Monica from CS so we can triage immediately.

Initial plan:
- Ben: immediate investigation of KV prefetch/priority preemption behavior for scitext-main; look for HOL (head-of-line) blocking and tenant preemption events.
- If we confirm tenant preemption / cache thrash we can temporarily route scitext to the low-latency variant (dedicated lane) or pin a warm prefix as a short-term mitigation.
- Monica/CS will coordinate customer communication and confirm if routing to a dedicated variant is acceptable from their side (billing/commit implications).

Daniel — do you authorize a temporary routing change (we can revert in <1hr) or would you prefer we first try a configuration tweak (prefetch throttle / kv slot priority) with a canary? If you approve routing we’ll also provide a follow-up credit if this is on our side.

I’ll update once Ben posts findings.

— Rafael
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel@scitext.ai>
Date: 2028-11-06T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden stream-start latency spikes, suspect multi-tenant interference

Quick triage notes (raw):
- Observed repeated KV eviction/preemption events tied to tenant prefetch spikes from a neighboring tenant pool (tenant-id: eu-thermal). When tenant eu-thermal ramps, it grabs hot slots and preempts scitext keys causing HOL waits while the KV subsystem reloads prefixes.
- Prefetch windows show overlapping async fetches that block head requests due to slot-level priority inversion.
- Sample log snippet: "kv_fetch: slot=47 tenant=scitext-main preempted_by=eu-thermal priority_preempt=1.00 delay=842ms"

Immediate mitigations I propose (ordered by risk/time-to-roll):
1) Emergency route: move scitext-main -> variant:dedicated-lowlatency-usw2 for 30m (fast; accepted by runtime). Requires Daniel confirmation.
2) Config change (canary 5% traffic): reduce prefetch parallelism + lower preemption threshold for eu-thermal-like tenants: rwctl set-prefetch-parallelism --tenant eu-thermal --value 2; rwctl set-kv-preempt-threshold --tenant eu-thermal --value 0.6
3) Medium-term: allocate tenant-affinity slots (isolate hot tenants) or adjust slot-ownership smoothing (config: kv_slot_priority_smoothing=120s) to reduce oscillation.

I can push (2) to 5% traffic in the next 12 minutes and monitor. If Daniel approves dedicated lane we can remediate immediately and then roll the config change out afterwards to prevent recurrence.

Logs/metrics attached for reference.

— Ben
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-06T10:28:00-08:00
Subject: Escalation: Scitext multi-tenant KV preemption impacting p95/p99 — exec sync

Grace — escalating for visibility. Summary: production tenant (Scitext) in us-west-2 is experiencing significant p95/p99 stream-start latency and a small but material 5xx rate due to KV preemption / cache thrash from an adjacent tenant. Ben confirms head-of-line blocking caused by priority preemption events.

Impact: customer-facing search queries failing intermittently; observed SLA risk for a customer on a growth plan. Customer asked for immediate mitigation; we recommended temporary routing to a dedicated low-latency pool while we implement a canary config fix.

Questions for leadership:
- Approve one-hour routing to a dedicated lane for scitext (will impact capacity; potential short-term MRC discussion).
- Approve proactive credit to the customer if root cause is our multi-tenant scheduler / prefetch behavior.

Timeline: Ben can push a 5% canary config in ~12 minutes. Dedicated routing is available now and can be reverted. Monica is on the thread for customer communication.

Requesting a quick yes/no so we can move.

— Rafael

From: Daniel Park <daniel@scitext.ai>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@scitext.ai>
Bcc: ops@scitext.ai
Date: 2028-11-08T17:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: Scitext multi-tenant KV preemption impacting p95/p99 — exec sync

Thanks Rafael & team — appreciate the quick triage. We authorize routing scitext-main to the dedicated low-latency variant immediately. Please confirm expected timing and any billing implications; our procurement lead (Priya) is CC'd. We also want the canary config pushed as soon as the routing is stable so we don't rely on the dedicated lane longer than necessary.

High level ask: a short postmortem with timeline and a proposed fix to avoid recurrence (isolation vs smoothing). The Drive link in your earlier email for logs/next-steps is fine.

We’ll expect an initial status update in 30 minutes and a postmortem within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Daniel
